headline: The more conventional RBS-15 anti-ship missile carries a 200 kg semi-armor-piercing high-explosive fragmentation warhead and has a range of 200–300 km, depending on the variant, with a top speed of approximately 1,100 km/h. During the cruise phase, it is guided by GPS/INS, while in the terminal phase an active radar seeker takes over, with the ability to home in on sources of electronic jamming. No public announcements had been made regarding the delivery of these missiles to Ukraine either. Their first confirmed appearance was in a low-quality video published on April 6, marking the first observed use of the system.

headline: The low-observable Naval Strike Missile (NSM) carries a 120 kg penetrating warhead and has a range of 200–300 km, depending on the variant, with a top speed of approximately 1,100 km/h. During the cruise phase, it is guided by GPS/INS in combination with Terrain Contour Matching (TERCOM), which compares the terrain below with a preloaded digital map. In the terminal phase, a passive imaging infrared (IIR) seeker with automatic target recognition (ATR) takes over to engage the target. Plans to supply these missile systems to Ukraine had been discussed since 2023, but until now there had been been no official confirmation that they had been delivered.

The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene despite life-saving efforts by two National Guard medical specialists. No law enforcement personnel were injured. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation is leading the investigation. The incident marks the first fatal shooting involving National Guard personnel deployed under the administration's crime-reduction mission in Memphis, where the federal deployment has faced legal and political opposition since it began last year. Paris received €15.1bn instead of the €16.2bn it requested from the EU's €150bn SAFE fund, after some Franco-British projects, particularly involving missile maker MBDA, were deemed ineligible. The rules require 65% of funded defence products to originate within the EU, plus Norway, Iceland, or Ukraine. Since the UK has not finalized an agreement to contribute financially to the scheme, many joint UK-EU defence projects cannot qualify. Source: FT
